## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
*Hetuduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 9.1) is an Abhidhamma text belonging to the *Paṭṭhāna* collection [SuttaCentral]. Within the architecture of the *Paṭṭhāna*, it constitutes the opening section of the *Duka-Tika-Paṭṭhāna*, which systematically combines the dyadic classifications (*duka*) with the triadic classifications (*tika*) [Nyanatiloka 2007]. This specific text examines conditional relations at the intersection of the Root Dyad (*hetu-duka*) and the Wholesome Triad (*kusalattika*) [Nyanatiloka 2007].
Methodologically, the text expounds conditioning permutations across root and wholesome phenomena. As summarized by Nyanatiloka, it investigates positive relational questions such as: dependent on a phenomenon that is both a root and wholesome, there may arise—conditioned by way of root or other conditions—a phenomenon that is a root and wholesome, not a root but wholesome, or both a root and not a root together [Nyanatiloka 2007]. It likewise analyzes negative conditional permutations, such as *hetuduka-kusalattike nahetuduka-kusalattika* ("Dependent on a phenomenon which is a root and which is wholesome, there may arise a phenomenon which is a not-root and not-wholesome, conditioned by way of root") [Nyanatiloka 2007].
SuttaCentral records no curated parallels in early Buddhist or non-Pali traditions [SuttaCentral]. Machine analysis by DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse comprising 1,391 matches across 116 Pali texts, reflecting the standardized formulaic matrix of the *Paṭṭhāna* [DharmaNexus]. Its closest textual alignments occur with other combinatorial sections of the same treatise, notably *Hetuduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.1; 122 matches), *Hetuduka, Duka* (Patthana 6.1; 77 matches), and *Kusalattika, Hetuduka* (Patthana 10.1; 50 matches), as well as the post-canonical *Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā Abhidhammapiṭaka* [DharmaNexus]. Computational cross-language alignments detect faint, non-canonical overlaps with Tibetan translations of the *Āryasaṃdhinirmocanasūtravyākhyāna* and the *Yogācārabhūmi* [DharmaNexus].
